observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show a curved computer monitor displaying a webpage with product listings. The screen has a visible vertical black line running from top to bottom, as described by the seller.
The monitor is placed on a desk with cables and a mug visible in the background. The screen is split into two sections, suggesting a dual-screen setup or a wide display.

Photo 2 shows an open cardboard box with white foam packaging. Inside, there is a circular plastic-wrapped object (likely the monitor's stand or base), a manual, and a small plastic bag with accessories (possibly cables or adapters).
No brand or model name is visible on the monitor bezel or screen in any photo.
The watermark 'GIGAXYSAFE TECHNOLOGIES' is present on all photos, indicating the seller or listing source.

claims.claim: There is a thick vertical black line running from the top to the bottom of the screen.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and Photo 1 clearly show a vertical black line on the screen, running from top to bottom.

risks.risk: The vertical black line may be a permanent screen defect (dead pixel column or panel damage), which affects usability and value.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen showing the line under different brightness levels or with a solid color background (e.g., white or black) to confirm if it's a hardware fault or a software artifact.
risks.if_unproven: priced as defective, with reduced value due to screen damage

risks.risk: The monitor may not be in working condition or may have other unseen faults (e.g., backlight issues, input problems).
risks.proof: A video clip showing the monitor powered on, displaying different content (text, video, color bars) and connected to a device, to verify functionality.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working, with no functional guarantee

risks.risk: The monitor may be a counterfeit or non-branded unit, or the model may be misrepresented.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the back of the monitor showing the brand name, model number, and serial number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic or unbranded, with lower value

proof_requests: A close-up photo of the screen showing the vertical black line under a solid white or black background to confirm the nature of the defect.
A video clip of the monitor in use, displaying various content to verify functionality.
A clear photo of the back of the monitor showing the brand, model, and serial number.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a curved computer monitor, and the seller's claim about the vertical black line is supported by the photos. However, the nature of the defect, the monitor's functionality, and its brand/model are unverified. Without proof of these, the item cannot be priced accurately and carries significant hidden risks.
